items.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The band was playing. I walked up to -- Ernie Wilkins and Jimmy recognized me immediately.

ctx.x: Yeah, that’s the Detroit connection if you will, yet the Wilkins brothers were originally from St. Louis. Jimmy was the leader. The most noteworthy member of the band was a gentleman by the name of H. D. Whalem, who played tenor saxophone and played trumpet and sang. He was one of the most popular gentleman on the campus, because a singer gets all the glory. He sang in the Billy Eckstine -- then he could turn around and play a mess of tenor saxophone. Then he could turn around a play a mess of trumpet. So he was…
